dialogues.speaker: Frejus
dialogues.text: So, what did you think of the cannon?

choices.text: It could still do with a little work...

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: What do you mean?

choices.text: Well, it's stuck in one place...

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: I wasn't expecting a request like that... I guess I should have known someone as exceptional as you would have extraordinary ideas.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: But if I'm going to make it mobile, I'll need to do something about the recoil first.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: It is a naval cannon, after all. Of course, if it were you carrying it, I'm fairly confident you could withstand the force...

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: But for a regular member of the Gardes... the recoil would probably kill them stone dead. I'll need to invent a... "Miniature Terrestrial Naval-Grade Platform"! Something mobile that can support the cannon's weight.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Obviously, for something this big, I'll need to consider its defensive capabilities — armor plating would make it too heavy. Then, I need to consider propulsion and mobility. There's much to consider.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: The engineering designs are going to get extremely complicated. I wonder, can I really do this? I was rejected three times by the Fontaine Research Institute, and...

choices.text: I'd rather be able to pick it up and fire from different angles...

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: So you still remember me? That's wonderful!

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: It was a good while ago now, but you helped me test the original prototype for this cannon.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Back then, I was still lying to Chenee about being a genius...

choices.text: So, she finally figured you out?

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Haha, as it happens, the answer is neither — the lie evolved!

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Thanks to you, my cannon performed outstandingly, and the Maison Gardiennage rewarded me with financial support. They even introduced me to a few engineers.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: With guidance from those old hands — and after getting to grips with a fair few abandoned projects from the Fontaine Research Institute — I managed to produce some noteworthy inventions...

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Such as my "Shallow-Earth Mining Drill" and "Variant Antoine Roger Aircraft"... which I should really call the "Frejus Flyer."

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Of course, Chenee's favorite is the "Automatic Breakfast Oven." She uses it every day.

choices.text: So, in the end, your lie became the truth?

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Not at all. Everything I've invented was based on the work of others. I'm more of an improver than an inventor. If you were feeling particularly unkind, you might say all I do is "embellish" others' ideas.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: A real genius wouldn't need to borrow inspiration from anyone else.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: That said, I'm no longer that old run-of-the-mill everyman who couldn't make something valuable to save his life either.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: So I've come to feel that my "lie" has gradually evolved into more of a... a "promise," perhaps?

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: It's not quite so far from the truth anymore, but at the same time, I've still got some ways to go.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: I'll try my hardest! Your encouragement has given me a little more confidence.

choices.text: Perhaps you really were a genius all along?
Does that mean you came clean?
I need some more time to test it out.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Be my guest! The barrel's extremely durable, so fire away!
